statements.t: Our platform is designed to evaluate and integrate multiple analytes, including DNA, RNA and proteins, using differentiated laboratory automation capabilities and clinical studies to develop tests intended to address the biological heterogeneity of cancer.
We plan to seek FDA approval for SimpleScreen Lung.

We have incurred and expect to continue to incur recurring expenses associated with operating as a public company, including directors’ and officers’ liability insurance, director compensation, and increased accounting, legal, compliance, administrative, personnel, audit, and other professional service costs.

We receive milestone payments and expect to receive royalties under the arrangement.

We expect to fund our cash needs through cash on hand, cash generated from operations, if any, and, as needed, equity offerings, debt financings or other capital sources, including collaborations, licenses, royalty financings and similar arrangements.
As of September 30, 2026, we had $11.4 million of contract assets under the agreement, which we expect to bill in future periods.
Our cost of services will increase with commercialization of our products.
Research and Development (“R&D”) has been, and will continue to be, central to our business model.

In June 2026, in anticipation of FDA approval of our colorectal cancer screening test, we began capitalizing qualifying inventory costs associated with commercial production as we determined that future economic benefits associated with such costs were expected to be realized.
We expect our R&D expenses to continue to increase as we advance our technology platform, support additional product development activities, and conduct future clinical studies.

We expect to continue evaluating our development priorities and allocating resources among our programs based on nonclinical and clinical results, regulatory developments, and our ongoing assessment of each program's commercial potential.

We expect our general and administrative expenses to increase in future periods as we support the growth of our business, commercialize SimpleScreen CRC, expand our infrastructure and pursue commercialization of additional diagnostic test candidates, if approved.

As a public company, we also expect to continue incurring expenses for accounting, audit, legal, regulatory and tax services; Nasdaq and SEC compliance; directors’ and officers’ insurance; investor relations; and other public-company requirements.
As we expand commercial activities, we expect cost of services to increase as we incur and recognize costs associated with commercial products and testing.

Although we have completed the Business Combination and received the related proceeds, and our SimpleScreen CRC test has received FDA approval, we expect to continue to require substantial capital to support the commercialization of our approved product, advance our research and development programs, pursue additional regulatory approvals, expand our commercial infrastructure, and fund our operations.
